description:
From the fz-kdt.183 research (2026-09-03, d2a5f3510), proven at HEAD with no
prototype: two independent Enum.with_index statements; swapping their SOURCE
ORDER flips List.reduce_step/3's published ReturnType fact between
{:done, [binary]} and {:done, [int]} with an identical key and identical
row set. Cause: jobs/semantic.rs analyze_activation (:222-229) refines the
key-wide joined return by EACH ROW's @spec result in row order, and
refine_observed_return (:1884, :1903-1905) returns the observed type
unchanged when the intersection is empty -- so the first row's contract
narrows the join and every later row's contract is silently discarded.
fz-kdt.183's element-keyed fix removes THIS instance (the two rows become two
activations) but the mechanism survives wherever a key still shares rows
(the callable slot). Fix direction: a contract result may refine an
activation's return only when it is a fact about EVERY row the activation
carries (the meet over rows of each row's instantiated result, or nothing);
and an empty intersection is a diagnostic about the row, never a silent
no-op. Red-first: the swapped-order pair publishes the same fact.

comments.text: CONCORDANT with fz-kdt.65 (return-widening ladder resets only on rebase; join-only ascent) -- this is its join-only side made order-dependent by contract refinement. Also with fz-kdt.33 (spec enforcement waits for correlation-sound evidence). fz-kdt.183 removes the instance on List.reduce_step/3; the mechanism survives on any shared key.

title: A published return fact is source-order dependent: analyze_activation refines the key-wide join by each row @spec result in row order and refine_observed_return keeps the observed on an empty intersection, so the first row wins
